Abuse of Dominant Position: Undertakings holding significant market power can influence competitive conditions in the market more easily than their rivals. The abuse by dominant undertakings of this power in ways that restrict competition in the market is prohibited under Article 6 of the Competition Act (Law No. 4054). What matters in assessments under Article 6 is that a dominant position itself is not prohibited. An undertaking's market power may result from technological superiority, efficiency or a quality product/service.
Adil gelir dağılımı: The state in which the inhabitants of a country have equal opportunity in production and consumption and receive the share they deserve.
Adil sigorta poliçesi: An insurance policy whose premium is set to equal the expected value of that policy.
Administered Price: Prices set by undertakings or by the state that do not change in the face of short-term fluctuations in supply and demand conditions. According to some economists, this price rigidity stems from market power.
Ahlaki tehlike: The phenomenon of economic units making riskier choices when the cost of an adverse outcome will be paid by others.
Akreditif: A type of guarantee concerning the payment for exported goods, under which payment will be made once certain conditions are fulfilled. Banks or other financial institutions intermediate letter-of-credit transactions. Accordingly, a letter of credit is a kind of letter of guarantee sent by a financial institution to a correspondent bank in a foreign country, committing it to extend credit on its own account for a certain period, in a certain amount and in favor of a third party.
Aktif iş arama: Activities such as applying to an employment agency or directly to an employer, searching for work via the internet or newspapers, taking written or oral job examinations or interviews, and preparing to set up one's own business.
Akılcı beklentiler önsavı: The view that economic units take into account all past and forward-looking information when making forecasts about the future.
Akışkanlık ya da likidite: A conceptual measure describing how easily and quickly a financial asset can be converted into equivalent cash.
Algorithmic Collusion: An algorithm is expressed as a path designed to reach a goal, a set of steps followed; in computer science it is defined as the method by which software performs a task. Algorithms can, for example, be used by undertakings as a price-setting tool in online shopping. An undertaking can monitor a rival's product prices through algorithms and set its own prices accordingly. At a more advanced level, algorithms cease to be a tool of competition
Allocation of Common Costs: The allocation by a multi-product undertaking of its general expenses separately to the production costs of these products. While distributing general expenses among its products, the undertaking may take into account the demand elasticity of those products or the competitive constraints in the markets where they operate. For example, it may exclude general expenses from a product operating in a competitive market with high demand elasticity while keeping its price low in that market.
Alım Heyeti: A delegation of representatives of institutions and organizations, media members, producers and importers brought to the country to purchase goods or services, coordinated by the Ministry of Trade in cooperation with exporters' associations and/or organizing bodies, with the aim of increasing exports.
Alım Opsiyonu: It gives the option holder the right to buy the good, asset or financial indicator underlying the option at the price written in the contract at the contract's maturity, without incurring any obligation.
Alış: The price at which market participants are willing to buy assets traded in the market (such as foreign currency or securities).
Alış – Satış Farkı: Expresses the difference between the bid and ask prices of any traded security.
Amaç bağımsızlığı: The central bank's setting of its own monetary policy targets.
Amnesty Plus: Under the additional leniency rule, those who cannot benefit from the leniency program in an investigation concerning one market may, if they apply with respect to a cartel in another market, benefit from immunity for the second cartel and receive a reduction in the fines arising from the first cartel. In Turkish competition law, the provision on this subject is made in Article 7(2) of the Fining Regulation.
Ana faiz oranı: The rate that forms the basis of the interest banks charge for credit.
Anti-Competitive Agreements: Refers to the secret or open agreements of a restrictive nature on competition made among undertakings. Such agreements can be horizontal or vertical in nature.
Ara hedef: A target that can directly influence the main target of monetary policy and is more transparent and measurable than the main target.
Ara mal: Products that are used up in the production process or become part of a final good.
Aracı Kurum: Joint-stock companies authorized by the Capital Markets Board to engage in capital market activities.
Arakazanç Ticareti: Borrowing in a lower-interest (lower-cost) currency and deploying the loan by investing in a higher-interest (higher-yield) currency. The net return of the carry trade is determined by exchange rate developments, under the assumption that credit risk remains constant.
Aralık içinde dalgalanma: An exchange rate regime in which nominal exchange rates are allowed to move within a certain band around a central parity set by the central bank.
Araç bağımsızlığı: The central bank's setting of its own policy instruments to achieve its targets.
Arbitraj: The transaction of making a profit by simultaneously buying a security, currency or commodity in one market and selling it in another (exchanging the securities with one another). Arbitrage transactions lead to a reduction in price differences between markets. Today, with the growth of communication technology and the falling cost of accessing information, price differences between markets are extremely low, and any differences that appear are instantly eliminated by such transactions.
Artan fiyat ihalesi: Or the English auction: a type of auction in which participants make open bids and the price is progressively raised, starting from a low price, until the winner is determined.
Artan gider endüstrisi: An industry in which firms' average total costs rise as the market grows.
Artan oranlı vergilendirme: A taxation system in which the tax rate rises as the amount subject to tax increases.
Arz: A fundamental economic concept describing how much of a product sellers in the market want to sell, and can sell, in a given period.
Arz esnekliği: Or the price elasticity of supply, in short εS: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity supplied of a product changes as a result of a one percent increase in its price.
Arz eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity supplied, all else being constant.
Arz fazlası: Or surplus: the situation in which the quantity supplied in the market exceeds the quantity demanded.
Arz çizelgesi: A list showing how much of a product is supplied at different price levels in a given period.
Arz şoku: A change in aggregate supply in the economy due to an effect other than the general price level.
Arzın fiyat esnekliği: Or supply elasticity, in short εS: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity supplied of a product changes as a result of a one percent increase in its price.
Asgari geçim indirimi: The exemption of a certain portion of wages from tax.
Asgari ücret: The lowest wage set by the state as the compensation of labor for a certain period, which cannot be reduced by mutual agreement.
Asil-vekil sorunu: When the authority to carry out a transaction is delegated by the principal to the agent, the agent's acting in line with its own interests due to asymmetric information.
Asimetrik bilgi: The situation in which one of the parties to an economic activity has more information than the other.
Asit-test oranı: A liquidity ratio calculated from the current ratio by excluding inventories ((Current Assets − Inventories) / Short-Term Liabilities); it measures the most liquid items.
Association of Undertakings: Undertaking associations can from time to time direct their members through recommendation decisions in line with their founding purposes. Such recommendations may relate to sales prices and similar matters and may carry purposes and/or effects that restrict competition. It must be determined whether the recommendations of undertaking associations result directly in binding decisions of the association. Indeed, binding undertaking association decisions restrict competition
Assured Base of Sales: The core sales of undertakings refer to the sales they can make without feeling the competitive pressure of their rivals, as a result of factors such as brand image, product/service quality, accessibility and after-sales service quality. An undertaking having core sales means that a certain (inelastic) part of total demand in the market depends on that undertaking. Undertakings with market power are generally accepted to have core sales
Atık Bertaraf: The orderly and continuous storage of solid, liquid and gaseous wastes, their elimination by burning, and their conversion into products and energy for recovery. Preliminary Project: a draft prepared before the implementation project that gives an idea about the main project.
Avans: The transaction of lending against commercial bills and documents taken as collateral, as well as government bonds and exchange-listed bonds.
Average Total Cost: The costs obtained by dividing total costs, including variable and fixed costs, by the total quantity produced.
Ayni gelir: Non-monetary earnings provided to households in the form of goods and services by the state or employers.
Ayni Katkı: A contribution made in a project by the project owner and/or its partners in the form of land, goods, materials, labor, machinery and equipment to meet the project's specific needs. B2B: an abbreviation of Business to Business, this term refers to any commercial activity that businesses carry out directly with one another. B2C: an abbreviation of Business to Consumer, this term refers to any commercial activity that businesses carry out directly with consumers
Aynı kaynak için yarışan mallar: Products obtained from a common resource that can be used a limited number of times.
Ayrıştırma: Refers to the stripping of a coupon-bearing security so that its principal and coupons can be traded separately. The aim is, in particular, to broaden the scope of use of long-term coupon-bearing issues from the investor's perspective and to increase demand for such issues. For this purpose, the Undersecretariat of Treasury can strip the Government Domestic Debt Securities it has auctioned and the Lease Certificates it has sold directly into their principals and coupons.
Azalan fiyat ihalesi: Or the Dutch auction: a type of auction in which participants make open bids and the price is progressively lowered, starting from a high price, until a buyer emerges.
Azalan getiri yasası: A fundamental economic concept stating that while at least one production factor is fixed, the contribution to production of an increase in another variable factor will gradually diminish.
Azalan gider endüstrisi: An industry in which firms' average total costs fall as the market grows.
Azalan marjinal fayda yasası: A fundamental economic concept stating that as a product is consumed more within a given period, the additional utility obtained from it will gradually decrease.
Açık ekonomi: An economy that trades with the outside world to a considerable degree and establishes relations with it.
Açık gider: Expenses incurred directly in the course of economic activity and involving a specific payment.
Açık Mektup: A written text in which, pursuant to Article 42 of the CBRT Law, if inflation targets are not achieved or the possibility of not achieving them arises, the reasons for this situation and the measures to be taken are notified in writing to the Government and simultaneously announced to the public. The open letter is written, under the principles of transparency and accountability, when inflation occurs at a point outside the symmetric uncertainty band defined around the point target.
Açık piyasa işlemi: Or in short OMO: the central bank's buying or selling of securities from or to financial institutions for the purpose of monetary policy.
Açık Piyasa İşlemleri - APİ: Within the framework of the targets of monetary policy, the CBRT's transactions — in exchange for Turkish lira — of outright purchase and sale of securities, sale with a repurchase commitment (repo), purchase with a resale commitment (reverse repo), and the taking and giving of Turkish lira deposits, with the aim of effectively regulating the money supply and the liquidity of the economy. Through open market operations, central banks ensure that short-term interest rates form around the policy rate(s) and regulate liquidity in the financial markets.
Açık Pozisyon: The part of the assets held in a financial instrument such as foreign currency, gold or securities that cannot be met by liabilities of the same kind. For example, if 5 million US dollars of assets are held against a 10 million US dollar liability, the remaining 5 million US dollars represents the open US dollar position.
